acceptedAnswer.text: For a retail trading strategy: below 1.0 is weak, 1.0–2.0 is good (after all costs), 2.0–3.0 is very good, and above 3.0 sustained should make you suspicious, not proud. These are rough guides from third-party sources, never cutoffs; long-run buy-and-hold portfolios often sit at 0.3–0.6.

mainEntity.name: What is a good Sharpe ratio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Export your trade ledger, build a per-period series of net returns (after every Indian cost: brokerage, STT, exchange charges, stamp duty, GST), subtract the period risk-free rate (the RBI 91-day T-bill, cited as-of), and compute mean divided by standard deviation of the excess series — then annualize (×√252 for daily NSE data, ×√12 for monthly). In a spreadsheet on daily data: =AVERAGE(excess_range)/STDEV.S(excess_range)*SQRT(252).

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate the Sharpe ratio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sharpe divides excess return by total volatility, so it punishes upside wobble; Sortino divides by downside deviation only, ignoring the good months. For asymmetric strategies — trend following, options, anything that cuts losses and lets winners run — Sortino is the more informative companion, not a replacement.

mainEntity.name: Can the Sharpe ratio be negative?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because standard deviation counts all deviation from the mean, up or down — a huge winning month inflates the denominator and lowers the ratio. The formula cannot tell a +5% month from a −5% month; it only sees distance from average. This is the Sharpe ratio's first blind spot, and the Sortino ratio is its companion.

mainEntity.name: Why does the Sharpe ratio penalize upside volatility?

acceptedAnswer.text: The one you could actually earn risk-free: the RBI 91-day T-bill, auctioned weekly — about 5.56% cut-off at the 2026-10-14 auction, always cited with the as-of date. Never a copied US T-bill number, never a constant.

mainEntity.name: Which risk-free rate should an Indian trader use?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no industry consensus: platforms differ on the risk-free input, gross versus net returns, daily versus per-trade return construction, and whether they correct for autocorrelation. Internal comparisons and published research document gaps of 20–65% between computed Sharpe figures for the same strategy. Compute it yourself from your own ledger — a metric you cannot reproduce is not yours.

mainEntity.name: Why is the Sharpe ratio different on every platform?
